answer.sameness: Almost every page draws from the same rigid kit of 4 to 5 hero layouts: a 3-to-4-tile Bento photo collage with a solid coloured text block (avtoservis-mrak-gen, gostilna-pri-mostu-gen, pekarna-kvas-gen), a white-or-cream page with a two-column info/hours table in the hero instead of photography (cvetlicarna-marjetica-gen, salon-tina-gen, instalacije-rebernik-gen), an asymmetric split with a literary drop-cap paragraph under the right-hand image (fizioterapija-pregib-gen, gostilna-zlata-zlica-gen, zobozdravstvo-lebar-regen), or a photo top with a dark banner below. Mobile screens all share identical sticky bottom action bars ('Klic' + 'Navodila za pot' or a floating pin + 'Pokličite' pill) a…
recurringIssues: Several desktop heroes have zero photography and feel like bare directory listings with huge empty whitespace (instalacije-rebernik-gen, instrukcije-pia-gen, pizzeria-oljka-gen, racunovodstvo-seliskar-gen).
Fixed mobile bottom bars ('Klic / Navodila za pot' or floating pills) brutally collide with and obscure hero text, drop caps, and big year numbers across almost the entire batch.

The literary drop-cap paragraph tucked into the bottom-right of the hero (e.g. avto-kovac-regen, karoserija-hribar-gen, zobozdravstvo-lebar-regen) often gets clipped at the viewport edge and feels out of place on trade sites.
Hero headlines and dark banners are frequently clipped right at the bottom of the 1280x800 desktop frame (kmetija-grabnar-regen, elektro-zupan-regen, zobozdravstvo-lebar-gen).
Multi-image Bento grids look choppy and busy when packed with 3 or 4 small, similarly weighted photos in the first screen (frizerski-salon-mia-gen, kmetija-grabnar-gen).
Top navigation bars repeat the same two-button cluster ('Pokličite' + 'Navodila za pot') with identical pill/box styling across totally unrelated industries.

best.why: Warm, appetizing bakery colours and strong, well-composed sourdough photography make the Bento grid layout feel purposeful and craft-appropriate.
Rich dark palette, atmospheric barbershop photography, and balanced serif typography give it genuine local character and clear hierarchy.
The overlapping text card over a lush floral image, paired with a distinctive dusty-rose header, feels tailored to a florist rather than a generic trade.

weakest.why: The first screen is a sterile, photo-free white box with a tiny address table and vast dead space, offering zero visual appeal or trade credibility.
A pizzeria homepage with no food photography—just black serif text floating in an empty white rectangle—completely fails the business.
Looks like an unstyled word-processing document rather than a designed website, with weak hierarchy and awkward empty space.

answer.oneChange: Eliminate the photo-free 'text-and-table-only' hero template and stop reusing the exact same drop-cap editorial module and sticky mobile bottom bars across every client; instead, require every homepage to lead with strong, industry-specific visual art direction that fits neatly within the first viewport without clipping.
answer.summary: This portfolio is clean, legible, and avoids cheap stock-photo clutter, with sensible colour palettes and decent typography pairings (serifs for hospitality/craft, bold condensed sans for trades). However, looking at all 50 sites together exposes an assembly-line generator cycling through four rigid layout formulas. Too many '-gen' pages ship with zero hero imagery—a fatal flaw for a pizzeria, florist, or hairdresser—while another dozen lean on the exact same drop-cap paragraph trick regardless of whether the client is a mechanic or a dentist. Worse, the standardized mobile sticky bars cover up content on nearly every phone screen. Fix the viewport clipping, retire the text-only heroes, and vary your structural components.
